record_note: Every Cap. (ordinances and subsidiary legislation) in English, from the text in force on 1 July 1997 (or a later first version) to the last version dated on or before 2026-10-28 in the Department of Justice bulk files on DATA.GOV.HK; data retrieved 2026-10-28.

scope.when_absent: this corpus records no scope notes (no commit carries Applies:); the absence is not a statement that the change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: presumption against retrospective operation, and no retrospective criminal liability
default_reach.meaning: an Ordinance is presumed to operate from the day it takes effect and not to attach new legal consequences to events completed before then unless it says so; in criminal matters the Bill of Rights bars holding anyone guilty for an act that was not an offence when it was committed and imposing a heavier penalty than the one then applicable, and a lighter penalty provided later benefits the offender
default_reach.authority: Hong Kong Bill of Rights, Article 12(1) (Cap. 383 s. 8): "No one shall be held guilty of any criminal offence on account of any act or omission which did not constitute a criminal offence, under Hong Kong or international law, at the time when it was committed. Nor shall a heavier penalty be imposed than the one that was applicable at the time when the criminal offence was committed. If, subsequent to the commission of the offence, provision is made by law for the imposition of a lighter penalty, the offender shall benefit thereby."; the general presumption is common law and is not checked in this corpus
